name: Depolymerisation of PET (glycolysis, enzymatic)
applications: recycling coloured, multilayer or textile PET into new virgin-quality PET
principle: PET waste is broken back into its monomers or short fragments so that it can be purified and repolymerised into virgin-quality PET. Chemical routes such as glycolysis use glycol and heat; enzymatic routes use an engineered enzyme in water at moderate temperature. Carbios describes its C-ZYME process as solvent-free.

process_steps.name: Repolymerisation to PET
equipment: PET polymerisation line (at the host site)

performance.basis: Carbios, on Indorama Ventures' site; EUR 230 million

source.note: IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, 2025 assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Recycling via chemical depolymerisation for PET' 8

reference_plants.name: Carbios Longlaville plant, Meurthe-et-Moselle
reference_plants.status: ground-breaking April 2024; construction suspended pending project financing; the financial close target of 30 September 2026 was missed and the start of production, previously expected H1 2028, is postponed; credit committee approvals obtained from the majority of lenders during summer 2026, a commercial agreement with a major beverage-industry player being finalised to raise pre-sales to about 60% of nominal capacity, and due diligence by export credit agencies and equity partners ongoing (as of 24 September 2026)

source.note: Carbios press release, 3 August 2026; details from Carbios first-half 2026 results release, 24 September 2026

advantages: Gives virgin-quality PET from low-quality waste
Can accept coloured and textile PET
limitations: First commercial plant not yet running
Cost competitiveness against virgin PET not shown
